components.html:
About this build

This website is the first VomerLabs project: a place to show useful work, explain how it is made, and share what I learn. It is being built in the open, starting with the foundation and homepage.

The approach

Astro generates the pages as static HTML. Projects and lab notes live in Markdown or MDX files, with schemas checking their metadata. Plain CSS stays scoped to the component that owns it, with a small shared set of design tokens.

narrative.overview:
A calm, minimal, editorial home for an independent software studio. Warm off-white ground, near-black humanist type, gray-green supporting text, and thin rules make the work readable. Lime marks contact and actionable records; a softer lime distinguishes project status.

The system feels practical, curious, clear, and thoughtful. Large typography and open horizontal records create hierarchy without boxed project tiles. Content and ordinary links remain usable without JavaScript. The oversized homepage statement is an approved, deliberate expression of this world.
keyCharacteristics: Flat warm paper and restrained lime accents.
Locally served humanist sans with mono metadata.
Oversized statements balanced by quiet supporting text.
Open records, thin dividers, and generous shared gutters.
Small, purposeful state changes and visible keyboard focus.

rules.name: The Useful Lime Rule
rules.body: Use lime for actions, selection, and written project status; keep the page ground warm and quiet.

rules.name: The Statement and Record Rule
rules.body: Reserve the largest tight-tracked type for a clear statement or a real project title; let supporting explanations remain regular-weight and readable.

rules.name: The Open Record Rule
rules.body: Separate work with rules and spacing; preserve the unboxed record language established by the homepage.

dos: **Do** preserve the warm paper ground, ink hierarchy, and useful lime accents.
**Do** reuse local Kedebideri regular and bold, reserving mono for metadata and code.
**Do** keep the approved oversized statement and let surrounding whitespace support it.
**Do** show real work as open records with written status and clear ordinary links.
**Do** preserve visible keyboard focus, reduced-motion behavior, and readable source order.
donts: **Don't** turn open project records into raised, shadowed card grids.
**Don't** introduce eyebrow labels above the project record.
**Don't** use decorative glyph characters in place of the existing inline SVG arrow.
**Don't** invent projects, articles, results, or form interactions to fill space.
**Don't** shrink the approved display scale as a generic typography normalization.
